stories.headline: 2026 WNBA playoffs: How Jackie Young, Aces can pull even in semis
stories.summary: She's not a perennial MVP or "Point Gawd," but Jackie Young is as important as any Aces player as they enter Game 2 looking to even their semifinal series against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
Coach Becky Hammon glanced to her left and offered an apology she knew wasn't really necessary.

"Sorry about the 40," Hammon said to Las Vegas Aces guard Jackie Young, who had just played every minute of the team's series-clinching victory Thursday in the first round of the WNBA playoffs.

"If there's somebody who's going to do 40, it's her," Hammon said. "She's just built for these moments: physically built, mentally built, emotionally built."

Young has been that reliable since the Aces began this journey of eight consecutive WNBA semifinal appearances since 2019, the season she was drafted No. 1. She has appeared in 286 of the Aces' 292 regular-season games and all 59 playoff games since then. Over the past six seasons, Young has averaged more than 30 minutes per game.

Now as the defending champions seek to even their semifinal series against the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 on Wednesday night (9:30 ET), Young will be as important as any Aces player.

"She does everything really, really well on both sides of the ball," said guard Caitlin Clark, who played with Young on the U.S. World Cup team that won gold in Berlin in September -- and whose Indiana Fever lost to the Aces in the first round.

"She passes the ball and finishes through contact really well. She's strong, she's physical, she shoots the ball at a really high clip, too. I don't really think there's a single flaw in her game."

However, none of the Aces played very well in Sunday's 71-60 Game 1 loss to the Valkyries, with Young limited to 11 points on 4-of-15 shooting, with four rebounds and five assists. The Aces need Young to play more like herself if they hope to go back to Las Vegas for Game 3 tied 1-1.

Young has barely left the court in Las Vegas' first four playoff games, and likely won't for the remainder of the postseason. When there is a title up for grabs, Young is usually in the vicinity. She has won championships in high school, college and the WNBA, plus Olympic gold medals for Team USA in 3x3 and 5-on-5.

Now Young hopes to lead the Aces back to the WNBA Finals, where they could win a record-tying fourth championship.

Young is introduced in the starting lineup as "Special Agent Zero" at home games, a nod to her jersey number and an amusing Vegas-like moniker for a player whose game is rooted not in flashiness but in Midwest fundamentals. Born and raised in Princeton, Indiana, part of the greater Evansville area, Young was a prep superstar who went to Notre Dame and helped the Fighting Irish win the NCAA championship in 2018.

Young isn't the perennial MVP candidate like A'ja Wilson or the "Point Gawd" like Chelsea Gray, her teammates for the past six seasons in Las Vegas. Yet Young plays like an MVP and averaged the third-most assists in the WNBA this season.

"She's such a good scorer, they've got to bring a double on her," Gray said of the elevation of Young's elite playmaking. "I also think she's gotten riskier with her passing. It's not just a simple chest pass or a bounce pass. They're more difficult passes, and they're on time and on target."

Young had her best overall regular season this year, averaging career highs in points (18.9), assists (6.8), 3-pointers per game (2.3) and free throw percentage (92.8). She was key in the Aces' 2-1 first-round series win over the Fever, registering 18 points, eight rebounds and seven assists in the deciding Game 3.

"The ball is in my hands a little bit more this season, but it's also about making the right play," Young said. "It's just continuing to put in the work, and then just being confident.

"All the hours I've put into the gym to be able to play my game, and also watching film, the game has slowed down for me."

Young's belief in herself has grown since her three seasons with Notre Dame, where she averaged 12.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.5 assists. She was age-eligible to declare for the draft a year early.

That 2019 draft -- which included Asia Durr, Arike Ogunbowale, Napheesa Collier, Alanna Smith, Brianna Turner and Ezi Magbegor -- stands as one of the best in WNBA history. And even though she wasn't rookie of the year that season, needing more time to find her comfort zone with the Aces, Young has proved to be a worthy top pick from that talented draft class.

She has worked hard to improve different areas of her game. Young made 36 3-pointers at Notre Dame. She totaled just 22 in her first three WNBA seasons. That changed dramatically in 2022, when she made 50 and the Aces won their first championship. She has tallied 89, 70, 80 and 100 3-pointers since.

That required overhauling her shot mechanics, along with believing in herself. Former Notre Dame coach Muffet McGraw said the mental aspect of Young's growth as a pro player stands out to her more than anything.

Young set an Indiana high school career scoring record at Princeton with 3,268 points. But McGraw laughed remembering that when she watched Young then during the recruiting process, all she could think was, "Shoot more!"

"She was always passing, keeping her teammates involved," McGraw told ESPN. "Even here at Notre Dame, she was always someone who could do anything, but would kind of defer to other players.

"The biggest change Jackie has made -- and I credit her working with Becky for a lot of this -- is the mindset. Now she's coming down and pulling up for the 3, and I love it. I don't think she saw herself as, 'I'm the one.' Now she sees herself more in that role."

Hammon sees it, too.

"There's a certain presence that she carries with her, a certain assurance that she has in herself," Hammon said Tuesday of Young. "That kind of confidence can be contagious. With Jackie, it's interesting because she'll have these nights where she might be struggling. ...

"And then, boom, she'll go on a two- or three-minute run where she can have 15 points. That ability to take over a game is always there."

McGraw said Young moved the best without the ball among all the players she coached at Notre Dame, which has been nicknamed "Guard U" by WNBA followers because of its number of successful pro perimeter players. Young was also strong on defense as a collegian, something she has continued in the WNBA.

"It's hard to be the best defender and then also a top scorer and passer, too, because it takes a lot of energy," McGraw said. "But she's able to do that. She's just really smart. She can figure out how she needs to guard you. She knows your tendencies. She's always just in the right spots."

Young and the Aces have been right for each other the past eight seasons. She will be a free agent for 2027, and -- having just turned 29 in September -- will be coveted. But for now, her mind is on this series with Golden State and how to push the Aces forward. This is her time of year, and championships are her thing.

"It is special to have won at every level," Young said. "Somebody told me recently to try to enjoy that while I'm in it. So I try to think about all I've accomplished, while knowing there's still a lot more left."

Kendra Andrews contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Report: Alex Cora again declines chance to manage Phillies
stories.summary: Alex Cora once again has declined the opportunity to manage the Phillies, informing the club that he plans to take the 2027 season off, according to USA Today Sports.
stories.body:
Alex Cora once again has declined the opportunity to manage the Philadelphia Phillies, informing the club that he plans to take the 2027 season off, according to USA Today Sports.

Cora, who has been linked to the Philadelphia job since being fired by the Boston Red Sox earlier this year, recently spoke with Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski, USA Today Sports reported late Tuesday.

Dombrowski talked to Cora about becoming the Phillies' manager in 2027, but Cora -- who is still owed over $7 million from the Red Sox for the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million deal -- turned down the opportunity, according to USA Today Sports.

It marks the second time in less than six months that Dombrowski has offered Cora the Phillies' managerial job. The two connected in late April after the Phillies, who were off to a 9-19 start to the season, fired manager Rob Thomson.

Dombrowski acknowledged at the time that he offered the job to Cora, who had been fired by the Red Sox one day earlier. But Cora told Dombrowski that he wanted to spend the remainder of the 2026 season with his family, prompting the Phillies to pivot to bench coach Don Mattingly as Thomson's interim replacement.

The Phillies rallied under Mattingly, going 79-55 over the season's final five months and reaching the postseason as the National League's third wild card. Philadelphia was eliminated by the rival Atlanta Braves last week in the NL Wild Card Series.

The Phillies have not formally announced an update on the status of Mattingly, who reportedly also is a candidate for the full-time managerial role. Mattingly remains under contract with the Phillies as their bench coach for 2027, according to USA Today Sports.

Mattingly deflected questions about his future after the Phillies' season ended with their NLWCS Game 3 loss to the Braves last Thursday.

"It's not the time to talk about it," he said. "I'm comfortable with whatever they want to do.

"I want the best for the Phillies. I loved being in Philly this year. I actually like playing in that environment. I like the environment. It's a rough environment, but it's good."

Cora and Dombrowski worked together in Boston from 2015 to 2019 -- highlighted by the Red Sox winning the World Series in 2018, Cora's first year as manager.

"I think Alex Cora is one of the finest managers in the game of baseball," Dombrowski said in April. "I've been fortunate enough to work with Hall of Fame managers like Tony La Russa and Jim Leyland -- I've been very fortunate in my career. [Cora] has a chance to be in that same category, that's how good he is."

Cora went 620-541 in seven-plus seasons with the Red Sox, guiding them to three postseason appearances over that stretch.

Mattingly managed the Los Angeles Dodgers from 2011 to 2015 and the Miami Marlins from 2016 to 2022. He was the 2020 NL Manager of the Year after he led the Marlins to their first playoff appearance since 2003.

stories.headline: Why expansion to Houston makes too much sense for the NHL
stories.summary: Commissioner Gary Bettman said the league is considering a new team, and Houston's viability is concrete.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- Houston has been talked about as an NHL city before. There have been conversations, in group chats, on message boards and social media. Hockey fans have done it. So have Houston sports fans watching a game at any one of the several venues -- even during the time when the AHL was playing at Toyota Center.

The conversations still exist, but now they're louder and more real because the voices include the NHL, its stakeholders, a potential owner and figures within Houston's political and sports landscape about how the city could land an expansion team.

"I'm a big believer in that everything happens for a reason, right?" Harris County-Houston Sports Authority CEO Ryan Walsh said. "The right time, the right place, etc. Houston has been talked about as a destination for hockey for a long time. But I think Houston really is and has become a true destination for sports."

NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said in late June the league is exploring adding a second team in Texas, with Houston and Austin as potential targets.

Bettman said the league entered into an agreement with The Friedkin Group that gave them six months to explore putting a team in either city. It included agreeing to a $3.5 billion investment, including an expansion fee and building costs for an NHL arena.

In late September, Bettman said the NHL is not in a formal round of expansion, noting that the NHL board of governors has taken a "wait-and-see attitude" when it comes to adding expansion franchises. He said there is an expectation that he'll know whether the board of governors prefers Austin or Houston as a potential expansion target by the end of the year.

NHL deputy commissioner Bill Daly said there's a chance there might not be a vote on The Friedkin Group's bid by the NHL's next board meeting in December when the six-month exploration process has finished.

Houston's viability as an option is concrete. As is the interest from influential figures in the city. But, much remains fluid when it comes to whether the NHL chooses to go to Houston, Austin or remain with 32 teams until a later time.

For now, Houston remains the largest market in the U.S. without an NHL franchise. To get one would add to the city's distinction as one that heavily consumes sports. It already has MLB, the NBA, NFL, MLS and NWSL. Houston will see the return of the WNBA in 2027, with the Connecticut Sun relocating and becoming the Houston Comets.

With that many professional teams, two FBS programs in Houston and Rice, one of the nation's strongest high school sports scenes and a host for other major events such as the World Cup, Houston's status can be viewed as a double-edged sword. There's an argument that adding the NHL would make it one of the most complete sports cities in the nation. Another suggests there could be such a thing as too much sports, and how it would be challenging for an NHL team to find its footing.

Mainly, there are two questions at the heart of how Houston finds itself in this current position even when taking those differing perspectives into account.

Why Houston? And why now?

"Houston sells itself," Houston mayor John Whitmire said. "There are a lot of really fine cities, but there's only one Houston."

Houston's hockey history
Minor league hockey first came to Houston in 1946, but the team ceased operations in 1949. It returned in 1965 with the Houston Apollos. They were the Montreal Canadiens' farm team until 1969 when the team shuttered. The city got hockey back for a third time in 1972 with the arrival of the first iteration of the Aeros in the World Hockey Association.

The Aeros were in Houston for six seasons, won two league titles and were led by Gordie Howe along with his sons Mark and Marty.

"We knew absolutely nothing about Houston," Mark Howe said. "The first day we moved in -- Marty and I were still living at home at 18 and 19 -- I want to say there was a hurricane and you couldn't even see the house across the street. Then you go to the first day of training camp and it was 104 degrees outside. I think I sweated out 12 pounds."

Howe said the front office had the players out in the community to attract fans while teaching people more about hockey. It worked; the Aeros were in the top five of WHA attendance three times over a five-year period.

At the time, few U.S. cities had as many professional teams as Houston. The city was home to the Houston Astros, the Houston Oilers and the Houston Rockets.

"Football, for me, is obviously the biggest thing down in Texas," Howe said. "All the high schools played on Friday nights. If the Aeros played on a Friday night, we would probably be on page five or six of the sports section because of high school football. That's the way it was."

The Astros and Oilers called the Astrodome home. Even as Houston has changed and become much larger, there are still strong feelings about how the monument to advancement, which officially opened in 1965, remains the city's greatest achievement.

For some people, the Astrodome is what put Houston on the map at the same time as the city was putting a man on the moon. This is what sports means to Houston.

"They support everything and they're very proud of being Houstonians," said Tom Garrity, who was the president of the second version of the Houston Aeros for five seasons. "When you look at all their franchises, it's like anything. You have your ups and your downs. But I'd put Houston at the top of the list of supporting whatever is in town."

The WHA played its final season in 1979, with four teams -- the Edmonton Oilers, Hartford Whalers, Quebec Nordiques and Winnipeg Jets -- joining the NHL.

The Aeros disbanded a year earlier following the 1977-78 season.

In 1994, the IHL granted Houston an expansion franchise, reusing the Aeros name in homage to the former WHA team. The new Aeros won a league championship in 1999 -- but the IHL folded in 2001. The Aeros joined the AHL, and became the farm team for the Minnesota Wild. The Aeros also spent one season as a farm team for the Dallas Stars.

"It was a pretty traditional minor league hockey market. Weekend games were a way easier sell than a Tuesday night game," said Minnesota Wild broadcaster Joe O'Donnell, who spent five seasons with the Aeros. "You had a hardcore fanbase, a booster club, a season ticket holder base that was super passionate. Then, from a marketing standpoint, it was about how do you find a way to separate yourself and get the word out there."

Drawing fans was a gradual process. Eventually, the team reached the top five in AHL attendance. O'Donnell said one of the items that helped was the team playing its games at Toyota Center, home of the Rockets.

On the surface, the Aeros were playing in what might have been the nicest building in the AHL. They had future NHL players on their roster, won a league title in their second season and missed the playoffs only twice during their time in the AHL.

Why leave Houston?

"This is where the history of the owners of the Rockets and old Aeros comes into play," said David Walsh, a professor in the sports and fitness administration program at the University of Houston. "They were at each other's throats, egos, what have you. The old owner of the Aeros was Chuck Watson and the old owner of the Rockets was Les Alexander."

An arena rights battle... and the end of the Aeros
Watson owned the Aeros, and also operated The Summit, the arena where the Aeros and the Rockets played before moving to the Toyota Center. Alexander, who purchased the Rockets in 1993, tried breaking the lease agreement. Watson denied the move, and Alexander was forced to honor the original lease agreement that was set to end in 2003.

Alexander and Watson agreed to an arena deal in 1997 that gave both teams equal control, but Harris County voters rejected it in a 1999 referendum.

Around this same time, Alexander sought to purchase the Edmonton Oilers with the intent of moving them to Houston. The NHL already had expanded to seven markets before 2000, while three franchises moved to new cities. Moving the Oilers would have been part of a wave that saw two Canadian cities, Quebec City and Winnipeg, lose their teams to cities in the United States. The Oilers remained in Alberta with the Edmonton Investors Group purchasing the club in 1998.

In 2001, Alexander reached an agreement with the city to build the Toyota Center. The Summit, which was renamed the Compaq Center, was sold right as the original lease agreement ended in 2003. The same year, Watson sold majority ownership of the Aeros to the Wild's parent company, while staying on as a minority owner.

The Aeros moved to the Toyota Center, signing a three-year lease to become tenants of Alexander and the Rockets until 2006. Their second lease agreement was for a seven-year deal that ran through the 2012-13 season, but came with a significant rent increase.

Upon the expiry of the seven-year deal, it was reported that Alexander was seeking a 550% rent increase; instead, the Wild relocated the team to Des Moines, Iowa. Alexander later sold the Rockets to Tilman Fertitta, in 2017.

"I think he was very against any NHL team coming into Houston unless he owned it or owned part of it," David Walsh said.

How the HCHSA stabilized the market
Although the Rockets won back-to-back NBA titles, Houston's professional sports landscape was going through a challenging time during the 1990s.

Venues such as the Astrodome and The Summit were outdated. That led to tension between team owners and the city. In 1995, the Astros considered leaving for northern Virginia. In 1996, the Oilers relocated to Nashville to become the Tennessee Titans. Plus, there was the struggle between Alexander and Watson.

That led to Whitmire, then a state senator, helping establish the Harris County-Houston Sports Authority. The HCHSA was created to serve two purposes: Managing debt for professional sports venues, and attracting major sports events.

It became instrumental in the Astros building a new stadium, the NFL awarding Houston the Texans and the Rockets building a new home.

The venues for those three teams -- Daikin Park (named Enron Field when it opened), Reliant Stadium and Toyota Center -- opened within three years of each other in the early 2000s. The HCHSA also manages the debt for the Shell Energy Center, home of the Houston Dash and the Houston Dynamo, which opened in 2012.

Houston has also hosted the NCAA men's basketball Final Four, the College Football Playoff National Championship game, the Super Bowl and the men's 2026 World Cup.

The HCHSA has supported 130 sporting events since 2011 that have generated an estimated $4.3 billion in economic impact for the region.

"All in all, the sports authority has really helped create the fundamental parts and pieces of that foundation that make Houston a sports city," CEO Ryan Walsh said. "I think it's naturally a sports city anyway just based on our location, based on the interests that Houston has and the economy that we got certainly lends itself toward those participatory sports as well as consumer and spectator sports."

Don Lee, another professor in the sports and fitness department at UH, explained that there are several items that make Houston a viable option for an NHL franchise.

Houston has a proven professional sports infrastructure, further strengthened by the frequency of hosting major events.

The city also has the financial strength to support another team because of how much the city has grown economically over the past decade. Greater Houston's economic output has increased from $584.5 billion in 2014 to $785.3 billion in 2024, according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. It makes Houston the sixth-largest economy in the nation.

Census estimates put Harris County as the third largest in the nation behind Los Angeles County, California, and Cook County, Illinois. Those figures also reveal that Harris County has had the most population growth of any county in the nation since 2020, while Greater Houston has also had the most growth of any metropolitan area within the same window.

Greater Houston is the only metro in the top six that doesn't have an NHL team. Atlanta is the only other market in the top 10 that doesn't have one.

Adding Houston as a market could also serve another purpose for the league.

"The TV market is a big, big selling point for the NHL as they're going into negotiations for the next TV contract," Walsh said. "That seems very coincidental of looking at this in the here and now, and things starting to line up in places where in the past there were hurdles that were too tough to overcome, and other cities that might have been more palatable to go to."

The NHL's U.S. broadcasting rights deals with the Walt Disney Company and Turner Sports are set to expire after the 2027-28 season.

Lee pointed out that expanding to Houston would come at a time in which the league is seeing its Sun Belt teams thrive; six of the last seven Stanley Cup champions are from that part of the league's regional map.

"I think it can be a really interesting approach," Lee said.

Why an NHL team in Houston might not work
Houston has its strengths -- economic prosperity, population growth and countless entertainment and sports options -- but there are also disadvantages.

Whitmire admitted the city has its challenges much like other major U.S. cities. Houston has traffic problems, education challenges in its public schools and an aging infrastructure in a city that keeps growing.

"To solve problems you have to admit you have problems, and I'm not in the denial business," Whitmire said. "We've got challenges. ... We didn't get like this overnight. I know I've spent time saying what a great city it is and how prepared we are, but I am also honest enough to say that's why we would welcome a franchise because they will be our partners going forward.

"You'd like to think they need us and we definitely need them because that would contribute to that quality of life issue."

Another concern: Where the team fits within the overall entertainment and sports landscape.

Houston has developed a reputation of being a city that musical artists skip in favor of other cities such as Dallas or Austin. One of the items outlined in a Houston Chronicle story was how Houston has a "walk-up" mentality that sees fans deliberate if it's worth going to a concert.

David Walsh described it as "a psychic cost" fans throughout Greater Houston must weigh when it comes to their entertainment options.

"Let's say you want to go to a Texans game. Some things start running in your mind," he explained. "Obviously, the actual cost of the ticket. But then it's, 'How do I get the ticket? What about traffic? What about parking? What about food costs? I don't like crowds. Do I have to stand in line?' These are all these little hurdles that financially, mentally that might make that person say, 'Eh, I'd rather go to a movie tonight because it's right down the road.'"

Professional sports fans in Houston have been conditioned to drive downtown -- or just south of downtown -- to watch games. The Astros, Dash, Dynamo and Rockets play within two miles of one another in downtown Houston, while the Texans play eight miles south. And that can involve a frustrating amount of time in the car.

"In terms of a joking answer, it's every Houstonian's God-given right to be in traffic for an hour to go three miles," Ryan Walsh said. "Houston is known for a lot of things and one of them is we have a very expansive area. The area is growing even more. I've joked that College Station is going to be a suburb of Houston. But I don't think people mind traveling to see something they want to do."

The discussion around a potential arena site is one of the more intriguing questions. The Friedkin Group, which didn't respond to requests for this story, have remained tight-lipped regarding potential expansion.

Market saturation is another potential problem. After adding the NHL, the city would have seven teams in the major professional men's and women's leagues in addition to the collegiate and high school teams.

Ryan Walsh noted that each sport can attract a unique audience -- along with Houstonians who want to support the local team regardless.

"I was driving in this morning and saw a truck with a tow hitch cover that must have been custom made because it had the Rockets logo, the Texans logo, the Astros logo and the Dynamo logo on it," he said. "You're playing all the bases on that one, right? People in Houston just like sports."

Is Austin still in play?
There's also another potential obstacle facing Houston's bid for an NHL team: Austin.

The state capital has drawn interest for a number of reasons, principle among them growth.

The city of Austin reported that its population has gone from 656,562 residents in 2000 to what is expected to be 1,137,983 by 2030. Right now, 32% of residents came from other states, which would hypothetically include those who grew up in a hockey market.

One of the reasons for the growth is Austin's emergence as a tech hub. Dell Technologies, the Oracle Corporation and Tesla Inc. each have their respective headquarters either in Austin or its suburbs. The region has a $248.1 billion economic output, per the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.

Professional sports also work differently in Austin compared to Houston. Austin FC is the area's lone professional franchise, having begun play in MLS in 2021. The NHL would have a chance to be first of the largest four major professional men's leagues to be in the state capital.

"We look at the Chicago Bears. Would you have thought 20 years ago they would have gone to Indiana? No way," David Walsh said. "I promise you Hammond, Indiana, was a plan B or plan C. They will never admit it. ... But they gave them everything they wanted and more. And so if you don't treat Austin as a serious threat, then you're not understanding the sports world. So they are a serious threat because they can come in and say, 'We're going to give you everything and more.'"

The city is also home to the University of Texas, with one of the most passionate followings of any college or university in the nation. Austin hosts major events such as the annual Formula 1 United States Grand Prix and the NASCAR Texas Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas.

"If you're a UT fan, that's where you want to be," Whitmire said. "And UT sports is pretty outstanding. But they're not ... I'd say they're not professional sports. But now what they pay their football players is going to be hard to say it's not professional sports. Austin is a great city, but it's not Houston. It doesn't have our international communities. It doesn't have our diversity, and it doesn't have our sports venues."

As for Houston's chances? Whitmire said that there are no limits to what the city and the stakeholders will show as it relates to getting a team.

"I can't think of anything off the top of my head as long as it's lawful," Whitmire said. "We're not going to start selling dope out of an arena or anything. But if it's lawful, we'll pull that trigger."

stories.headline: Fantasy football matchup rankings: Upgrade D'Andre Swift, fade James Cook III
stories.summary: The most and least favorable matchups in the NFL for this week's games at the four key fantasy positions.
stories.body:
Making tough lineup decisions each week can be the most challenging part of fantasy football. When you're torn between two similar players, start the player with the superior matchup.

But exactly how does one determine the best (and worst) weekly matchups?

The matchup rankings provide a schedule-independent method to evaluate positional matchups, ranking all 32 opposing defenses in order of most to least favorable for opposing players at all four skill positions. Instead of relying upon seasonal totals, we calibrate points-allowed data to show how each defense fared relative to the difficulty of the schedule it has faced.

For Week 5, 2026 full-season data is used, and once five weeks are in the books, only the most recent five weeks' numbers will be used.

"Adj. FPA," or Adjusted Fantasy Points Allowed, reflects how far above or below players' weekly PPR fantasy point averages that defense held opponents at that position. A positive number means that the matchup is favorable; a negative number means it is unfavorable.

Finally, a caveat: Matchups are only one ingredient in my rankings formula. Not every favorable matchup should be exploited, nor unfavorable matchup avoided. If you want the most complete source for whom to start, consult our weekly rankings.

Quarterbacks

Matchups highlight: Jared Goff, Detroit Lions (at Arizona Cardinals). Lions games have been extremely conducive to big passing numbers. They've been involved in four of the nine games with the highest over/unders, with all of them going over, and they've run the fourth-most passing plays while allowing the second most. This is another of those lofty over/under games (54.5), and it involves a Cardinals defense that surrendered a combined 67.28 fantasy points on passing plays to Drew Lock, Brock Purdy and Jameis Winston the past three weeks. This might well be one of those games where scads of passing yardage piles up in the closing minutes.

Others to like:

Jacoby Brissett, Cardinals (versus Lions)

Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams (versus Buffalo Bills, Monday Night Football)

Matchup to avoid: Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers (at Seattle Seahawks). The Seahawks, outside of their seemingly inexplicable 33-31 loss at home to Marcus Mariota and the Washington Commanders, have been a headache matchup for opposing quarterbacks. They held each of Drake Maye, Brissett and Justin Herbert under 10 fantasy points while creating seven total turnovers against them. Purdy himself struggled against the Seahawks in their two meetings last season, scoring 21.96 total fantasy points while committing three turnovers.

Running backs

Matchups highlight: D'Andre Swift, Chicago Bears (at Green Bay Packers). Kyle Monangai's Week 4 outburst casts the Bears' division of carries into question, but with Monangai exiting that game with a thumb injury, it might serve the team best to shift more of the work back to Swift, even if only for the week. A soft matchup against the Packers seems like a smart place to do it. The Packers have surrendered the third-most fantasy points (29.0 per game), points per rushing attempt (0.80) and points per target (2.12) to running backs, and much of that was accrued before the team lost LB Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending Achilles' tear in Week 4.

Others to like:

Quinshon Judkins, Cleveland Browns (at New York Jets)

Emanuel Wilson, Seahawks (versus 49ers)

David Montgomery, Houston Texans (at Tennessee Titans)

Matchup to avoid: James Cook III, Bills (at Rams). It's rare that he'll land on this side, and in no way does his place here say, "Sit James Cook III, he's so much worse than Emanuel Wilson!" Cook is one of the more heavily involved running backs -- 11th in snap (68%) and 10th in rushing shares (64%) -- but it's the matchup, and how it further complicates his quest for touchdowns, that detracts. The Bills have run the football nine times inside the opponent's 3-yard line, and Josh Allen has six of them, converting all six for scores. The Rams, meanwhile, have yet to allow a touchdown or a 15-fantasy-point game, to a running back this season.

Wide receivers

Matchups highlight: Michael Wilson, Cardinals (versus Lions). Lions opponents are no worse for wear in terms of passing offense than they are, as the team has surrendered the second-most fantasy points per game (44.0), Adjusted Fantasy Points Added (+7.8) and fantasy points per target (2.12) to wide receivers thus far. Opposing WR1s have been especially dominant against the Lions, as Chris Olave, Garrett Wilson and Tetairoa McMillan averaged 14 targets and 33.4 fantasy points in their meetings. True Cardinals "WR1" Trey McBride also matches up brilliantly for this game, but Wilson's usage says he should be no slouch. Wilson is sixth in the league in target share (29%) and fifth in red-zone targets (8).

Others to like:

Carnell Tate, Titans (versus Texans)

Jameson Williams, Lions (at Cardinals)

Dontayvion Wicks, Philadelphia Eagles (at Jacksonville Jaguars, in London, Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET)

Matchup to avoid: Christian Watson, Packers (versus Bears). The No. 5 wide receiver in fantasy scoring, not to mention No. 6 in yards after the catch per reception (6.5) and No. 4 in red-zone targets (7), Watson is sure scripting a brilliant breakthrough story. But he might find success tougher to come by against the Bears, a defense that has been exceptional against wide receivers over the past three weeks. In that time, Justin Jefferson, DeVonta Smith and Wilson have averaged 22.3 routes, six targets and 8.9 fantasy points.

Tight ends

Matchups highlight: Isaiah Likely, New York Giants (at Commanders). The Commanders have struggled mightily against the pass this season, just as they did in 2025 (29th, with +3.5 Adjusted FPA against tight ends). They're especially weak against tight ends, who have averaged a league-high 2.93 fantasy points per target against them. Dallas Goedert, Jake Ferguson, AJ Barner and Tyler Warren averaged just 5.8 targets, yet averaged a whopping 16.3 fantasy points against this defense in their meetings. Likely is a top-five tight end for Week 5 facing this matchup.

Matchup to avoid: Dalton Kincaid, Bills (at Rams). Before we declare the Kincaid magic done, bear in mind the matchups. He has faced the Nos. 1 (LAC) and 3 (NE) schedule-adjusted defenses against tight ends the past two weeks, which helps explain his totals of five targets and 5.5 fantasy points in those games. Kincaid next faces the Rams, fourth toughest on the matchups list, and a defense that has afforded the position the fewest fantasy points per target (0.91).

stories.headline: Tottenham's Mathys Tel equals France under-21 goalscoring record
stories.summary: Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.
stories.body:
Mathys Tel will be hoping to take his goal-scoring exploits with France Under-21s over the international break into Tottenham's fight to turn their Premier League season around.

Tel has yet to score for Spurs this season but hit a hat-trick in a 7-1 win over Switzerland in Orleans on Tuesday night as France, who had already qualified for the 2027 European U21 Championship, completed their group campaign unbeaten with eight victories.

With 17 goals, Tel, who also scored in two other games over the break, has equalled Odsonne Edouard's record for France U21s and could have put himself into contention for a senior call-up to Zinedine Zidane's squad for the Nations League games in November.

"My brother had been nagging me about it [the goals record] for months. In the end it was in the back of my mind," Tel told reporters, as quoted in L'Equipe.

"With qualification [achieved], there was a different kind of motivation that allowed me to give my best, so now I am very happy."

Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham slumped to the bottom of the table ahead of the international break, with a 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa a third loss from their five opening Premier League games.

The boss welcomed former player and first-team coach Gus Poyet to the training ground on Tuesday and appeared in good spirits as the pair chatted on the sidelines in a video on the club's social media account.

Spurs travel to Manchester United on Saturday and have a few fitness concerns following the international break.

Right-back Pedro Porro has been carrying a hamstring injury which saw him pull out the Spain squad ahead of the extended three-week window.

Defender Jan Paul van Hecke was then sent home early from the Netherlands camp with a foot problem, which could keep him out of contention at Old Trafford.

Fellow Dutchman Micky van de Ven picked up a minor hand injury after being accidentally stepped on during the win over Serbia in Eindhoven and was forced off late on, but the Spurs captain is expected to be involved.

Speaking after the match, Netherlands manager Xavi told reporters: "He is okay. He felt dizzy because he suffered with his finger. It is not a big injury."

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 40
Goals: 36
Assists: 17

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami

Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Mercedes confirm George Russell engine penalty at Singapore Grand Prix
stories.summary: Mercedes has confirmed that George Russell will serve an engine penalty at the Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday.
stories.body:
Mercedes has confirmed George Russell will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to an engine penalty.

Russell retired from third at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia due to a power unit failure with six laps remaining.

Mercedes need to introduce replacement power unit to Russell's car in Singapore, which will take him above his quota of power unit components for the season and result in a back-of-the-grid penalty.

It is another setback to his championship hopes. His teammate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the F1 standings sits at 84 points, and Russell is second.

Team principal Toto Wolff's pre-race statement said: "George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty [in Singapore], which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia.

"That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for. Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport and our focus now is on giving him the best possible car and opportunities to fight back through the field."

After reliability issues earlier this year, Mercedes was already planning for Russell to take an additional power unit and the resulting penalty before the end of the season, but was not expecting to do so in Singapore where overtaking in the race is notoriously difficult.

The failure in Malaysia forced the team's hand as Russell does not have enough low-mileage components in his pool of engine parts to avoid taking a new power unit this weekend.

The situation is further complicated for Russell as Mercedes was planning to bring a performance upgrade to its power unit at the U.S. Grand Prix in two weeks' time, which the team had hoped would coincide with the introduction of Russell's final power unit of the year.

Mercedes has not yet confirmed whether the upgrade can be fast-tracked for introduction in Singapore or whether Russell will need to use older specification parts this weekend.

Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord warned in Malaysia that Russell may face a "double whammy" if he then has to take another penalty at the U.S. Grand Prix to access the upgraded power unit for the rest of the season.

Wolff also confirmed that his team will use this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix to assess the aerodynamic upgrades it brought to its car in Malaysia.

Despite expectations that the update would move the championship leaders comfortably ahead of its competitors, Max Verstappen's Red Bull proved to be fastest car at Sepang while Mercedes was left scratching its head over its relative lack of performance.

Wolff revealed his team would use the Singapore weekend to run direct comparisons between its previous aerodynamic package and the new updates.

"Malaysia was obviously a very difficult weekend for us," Wolff said. "We have spent the days since then working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been.

"We have identified several areas we need to investigate further, but F1 doesn't offer simple answers and we need more evidence before drawing firm conclusions.

"Singapore gives us an immediate opportunity to continue that work. The characteristics of the circuit are very different and that will help us build a clearer picture of where we are.

"That is why we will evaluate both the latest update package and our previous specification across the weekend to ensure we fully understand the direction we need to take."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Matchmaking, inactivity -- and, yes, fights -- shift MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
The fighter who won a UFC championship on Saturday does not move an inch in the ESPN divisional rankings. But several other fighters who did not even compete over the weekend do rise in their divisions' top 10s. One shifts from the top of one division's rankings to the middle of the pack in another weight class.

The new champion is Natalia Silva, who cruised past unranked Wang Cong at UFC 332 to capture the vacant women's flyweight title. Silva stays put at No. 2, however, below Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the title while recovering from injury.

Several other weight classes saw significant shifts, in some cases because of a lack of fights and in one case because of a fight booking for the future.

The most significant move is Alex Pereira shifting into the heavyweight rankings following the UFC's announcement that he will face Sergei Pavlovich on Dec. 12. It will be the second straight heavyweight fight for the former middleweight and light heavyweight champion, who has been No. 1 in the 205-pound rankings. He now moves to the heavyweight top 10, where he is ranked No. 7, two spots behind Pavlovich.

At light heavyweight, everyone previously below Pereira moves up, with ex-champion Magomed Ankalaev now No. 1. New to the top 10 are ninth-ranked Bogdan Guskov and No. 10 Robert Whittaker, as Khalil Rountree Jr. is out because he has not fought in over a year.

Also ineligible because of inactivity is middleweight Nassourdine Imavov, who is replaced in the 185-pound rankings by Christian Leroy Duncan. Perfect timing, as Duncan fights No. 5 Brendan Allen on Saturday's UFC card.

The other top-10 newcomer is men's bantamweight Payton Talbott, who knocked out Deiveson Figueiredo at UFC 332 to oust him from the rankings.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.
